messages.content: Write a conference talk abstract for a talk about moving a monolith to microservices. Around 200 words.

**We cut the monolith along the wrong seams. Twice.**

The books all say to start from bounded contexts. We did that. Eighteen months and forty-one services later, a single checkout request touched nine of them, and our p99 latency had tripled.

Microservices weren't the problem. The problem was that we drew our boundaries off a whiteboard sketch of how the business ought to work, rather than off what the code actually did at 3am on Black Friday.

This talk covers the second attempt, the one that worked. I'll show how six weeks of production traces exposed the real seams: the call paths that never crossed, the tables only one module ever wrote to. That evidence took us from a planned twenty-eight services down to eleven. I'll go through the strangler-fig plumbing (an nginx rewrite layer, plus a dual-write window we held open for four months), what we misjudged about distributed transactions, and the two services we folded back into the monolith because splitting them bought us nothing except pager noise.

You'll leave with a test for whether a given seam is worth cutting, and with permission to leave the rest of them alone.

*For engineers and architects who have read the theory and now have to ship it.*
